terms.meaning: A question that expects different answers across a group or over time, so it needs data.
The sum of the values divided by how many there are. Old Indian texts called it samamiti, the equal measure.
The middle number when the data is put in order.
A value much larger or much smaller than the rest of the data.
A number line with a dot above it for each data value.

items.name: Finding the mean
items.formula: Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values

items.name: Where the mean lies
items.formula: Between the smallest and largest values
items.example: The mean of 12, 15, 18, 19 is 16, which lies between 12 and 19.

items.name: Median of an odd number of values
items.formula: Put in order and take the middle one
items.example: 5, 2, 9, 7, 3 in order is 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, so the median is 5.

items.name: Median of an even number of values
items.formula: Take the mean of the two middle values

items.name: Outliers
items.formula: They move the mean much more than the median
items.example: 1, 2, 3, 4, 90: the mean is 20, but the median is 3.

items.name: A score of 0 and an absent match
items.formula: Count a 0, but leave out a match not played
items.example: Scores 40, 0, 20 in 3 matches: 60 ÷ 3 = 20. If the 0 was a missed match: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.

items.name: What a dot plot shows
items.formula: Tall stacks show the common values
items.example: Stacks of 1, 4 and 2 dots at 10, 11 and 12: the most common value is 11.

items.name: Comparing two groups
items.formula: Compare their means, medians and ranges
items.example: A smaller range means the values are closer together.

mistakes.text: Sort the values before finding the median. For 5, 2, 9 the median is 5, not 2.
Do not count a match not played as a 0. It leaves the count altogether.
The mean need not be a value in the data, and it need not be a whole number. The mean of 2 and 3 is 2.5.
